domain: CoreLocation — continuous life-logging of place (iOS 26 shipping / iOS 27 beta 4, verified against developer.apple.com JSON doc API on 2026-07-24)

capabilities.stream: Arrival/departure at a place (CLVisit: coordinate, horizontalAccuracy, arrivalDate, departureDate)
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.startMonitoringVisits() / stopMonitoringVisits(); CLLocationManagerDelegate.locationManager(_:didVisit:); CLVisit
capabilities.permission: Prompt: 'Allow While Using App / Allow Once / Don't Allow', then the Provisional-Always second prompt. Info.plist: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription + NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 8.0+ (NOT iOS 10 — Apple's platform table says 8.0; macOS 10.15+)
capabilities.resolution: Lowest-power primitive Apple offers. Apple publishes NO latency or accuracy figure. Events are opportunistic: an arrival event may carry arrival only; a departure event carries both arrival and departure ONLY if you were monitoring before the arrival. arrivalDate == Date.distantPast when unknown; departureDate == Date.distantFuture when unknown. horizontalAccuracy = radius (meters) of the circle centered on coordinate.
capabilities.backfill: none — no visit that occurred before you called startMonitoringVisits() is ever delivered
capabilities.notes: THE relaunch winner. Verbatim: 'If your app is terminated while this service is active, the system relaunches your app when new visit events are ready to be delivered. Upon relaunch, recreate your location manager object and assign a delegate to begin receiving visit events. You don't need to call this method again to restart the delivery of visit events.' Contrast SLC below — visits resume WITHOUT re-calling; SLC must be re-called. Also runs with NO precise-location request: 'Your app can monitor for visit events without calling requestTemporaryPreciseLocationAuthorization(withPurposeKey:). In that case, the visit events use reduced accuracy.' Requires Always for terminated-app relaunch. Apple's docs are SILENT on reboot behavior for visits (checked startMonitoringVisits, CLVisit, requesting-authorization, handling-location-updates-in-the-background).

capabilities.stream: Coarse position fix every ~500 m of travel (significant-change location service)
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges() / stopMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges() / significantLocationChangeMonitoringAvailable(); delegate locationManager(_:didUpdateLocations:)
capabilities.permission: Same as visits. Always required for terminated-app relaunch
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 4.0+
capabilities.resolution: Verbatim: 'Apps can expect a notification as soon as the device moves 500 meters or more from its previous notification. It should not expect notifications more frequently than once every five minutes.' Uses cellular/Wi-Fi, NOT GPS. distanceFilter and desiredAccuracy are IGNORED ('This property effects only the standard location services, not for monitoring significant location changes').
capabilities.backfill: none, but on (re)start the first delivered event is usually the most recently CACHED fix, and CLLocationManager.location is pre-populated before you start: 'the location property of your location manager object is populated with the most recent location object even before you start location services'
capabilities.notes: Relaunch semantics differ from visits. Verbatim: 'If you start this service and your app is subsequently terminated, the system automatically relaunches the app into the background if a new event arrives... the options dictionary passed to application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:) contains the key location... Upon relaunch, you must still configure a location manager object and CALL THIS METHOD to continue receiving location events.' Docs silent on reboot.

capabilities.stream: Continuous high-rate position track (CLLocation: coordinate, timestamp, horizontalAccuracy, verticalAccuracy)
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.startUpdatingLocation() + allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates + pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically + activityType + distanceFilter + desiredAccuracy; showsBackgroundLocationIndicator
capabilities.permission: WhenInUse is sufficient IF the app starts updates in the foreground. Info.plist: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription AND UIBackgroundModes array containing 'location'
capabilities.entitlement: none — UIBackgroundModes is an Info.plist array value, not a code-signed entitlement, so it works on a free personal team
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 2.0+ (allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates iOS 9.0+; pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically iOS 6.0+)
capabilities.resolution: desiredAccuracy constants (all 7): kCLLocationAccuracyBestForNavigation, kCLLocationAccuracyBest (iOS default), kCLLocationAccuracyNearestTenMeters, kCLLocationAccuracyHundredMeters, kCLLocationAccuracyKilometer, kCLLocationAccuracyThreeKilometers, kCLLocationAccuracyReduced. distanceFilter default = kCLDistanceFilterNone (report all movement); CLLocationDistanceMax also defined. CLActivityType (all 6): other (default), automotiveNavigation, fitness, otherNavigation, airborne, maritime.
capabilities.backfill: none — while suspended the system 'enqueues location updates and delivers them when the app runs again', so you get a burst on resume, but nothing from before you started
capabilities.notes: DOES NOT RELAUNCH. Verbatim: 'If your app is terminated, the delivery of new location events stops altogether.' FATAL-ERROR TRAP, verbatim: 'Setting the value [allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates] to true but omitting the UIBackgroundModes key and location value in your app's Info.plist file is a fatal error that terminates the app.' PAUSE TRAP: pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically defaults to TRUE on iOS and, verbatim, 'For apps that have in-use authorization, a pause to location updates ends access to location changes until the app launches again and is able to restart those updates.' Apple's own workaround: disable it and set kCLLocationAccuracyThreeKilometers when backgrounding. showsBackgroundLocationIndicator affects only Always-authorized apps; WhenInUse apps ALWAYS show the blue indicator in background.

capabilities.stream: Modern async position stream with per-update diagnostics (CLLocationUpdate)
capabilities.api: CLLocationUpdate.liveUpdates(_:) -> CLLocationUpdate.Updates (AsyncSequence). Properties: location, isStationary {DEPRECATED}, stationary, accuracyLimited, authorizationDenied, authorizationDeniedGlobally, authorizationRequestInProgress, authorizationRestricted, insufficientlyInUse, locationUnavailable, serviceSessionRequired
capabilities.permission: Iterating the stream itself triggers the prompt. Core Location sets WhenInUse implicitly when you process CLLocationUpdate/CLMonitor events or hold a CLBackgroundActivitySession
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 17.0+ (struct and liveUpdates); the diagnostic booleans stationary/insufficientlyInUse/serviceSessionRequired are iOS 18.0+ — accuracyLimited/authorizationDenied/authorizationDeniedGlobally/authorizationRequestInProgress/authorizationRestricted/locationUnavailable also arrived post-17.0
capabilities.resolution: CLLocationUpdate.LiveConfiguration (all 6): default, airborne, automotiveNavigation, fitness, otherNavigation, maritime. NO distanceFilter equivalent. Community measurement: ~1–2 updates/sec in foreground (twocentstudios, 2024-12-02, unverified by Apple).
capabilities.notes: PARTIAL means: runs in background only while a CLBackgroundActivitySession (and, for Always, a CLServiceSession) is held; it does NOT survive termination on its own. Apple: 'If your app actively receives and processes location updates and terminates, it should restart those APIs upon launch in order to continue receiving updates. When you start those services, the system resumes the delivery of queued location updates. Don't start these services at launch time if your app's authorization status is undetermined.' isStationary is now deprecated in favour of stationary. Field report: iOS 17 liveUpdates is unreliable (no results when full accuracy denied; missing diagnostic properties) — target iOS 18+.

capabilities.stream: Background-execution grant that lets a WhenInUse app keep logging after backgrounding
capabilities.api: CLBackgroundActivitySession() / invalidate() / diagnostics; CLBackgroundActivitySession.Diagnostic booleans: authorizationDenied, authorizationDeniedGlobally, authorizationRequestInProgress, authorizationRestricted, insufficientlyInUse, serviceSessionRequired
capabilities.permission: WhenInUse only — this is the point. Shows the blue background-location indicator instead of requiring an Always prompt
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 17.0+ (class and init); .Diagnostic is iOS 18.0+
capabilities.resolution: n/a — it is a session grant, not a data stream
capabilities.notes: Verbatim: 'An object that manages a visual indicator that keeps your app in use in the background, allowing it to receive updates or events... Use CLBackgroundActivitySession to start a background activity session that allows a when-in-use authorized app to receive location updates or monitoring events.' Must be recreated on relaunch — Apple's SwiftUI sample persists a UserDefaults flag ('BGActivitySessionStarted') and reinstantiates it in application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:).

capabilities.stream: Declarative authorization goal + authorization diagnostics (the modern Always upgrade path)
capabilities.api: CLServiceSession(authorization:) / (authorization:fullAccuracyPurposeKey:) / invalidate() / diagnostics; CLServiceSession.AuthorizationRequirement: always, whenInUse, none; CLServiceSession.Diagnostic booleans: alwaysAuthorizationDenied, authorizationDenied, authorizationDeniedGlobally, authorizationRequestInProgress, authorizationRestricted, fullAccuracyDenied, insufficientlyInUse, serviceSessionRequired
capabilities.permission: Creating the session IS the request. Suppress auto-prompting by adding CLRequireExplicitServiceSession to Info.plist
capabilities.resolution: n/a
capabilities.notes: Verbatim: 'If your app always needs authorization, it needs to create and hold a privileged session offered by CLServiceSession. This class provides a SINGLE OPPORTUNITY to upgrade from "While using" to "Always."' Also: 'If your app terminates, you must recreate the CLServiceSession immediately upon launch in the background.' DOC INCONSISTENCY worth knowing: 'Handling location updates in the background' names the opt-out key NSLocationRequireExplicitServiceSession while 'Suspending authorization requests' names it CLRequireExplicitServiceSession — same feature, two spellings in Apple's own docs.

capabilities.stream: Geofence enter/exit at named places (modern condition monitoring)
capabilities.api: CLMonitor(name) async; add(_:identifier:), add(_:identifier:assuming:), remove(_:), record(for:), identifiers, events; CLMonitor.CircularGeographicCondition(center:radius:); CLMonitor.Event (date, identifier, state, refinement + 10 diagnostic booleans: accuracyLimited, authorizationDenied, authorizationDeniedGlobally, authorizationRequestInProgress, authorizationRestricted, conditionLimitExceeded, conditionUnsupported, insufficientlyInUse, persistenceUnavailable, serviceSessionRequired); CLMonitor.Record (condition, lastEvent); CLMonitoringState: Satisfied, Unsatisfied, Unknown, Unmonitored
capabilities.permission: WhenInUse works with a CLBackgroundActivitySession; Always required for cold-launch relaunch
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 17.0+ (conditionLimitExceeded / persistenceUnavailable / insufficientlyInUse are iOS 18.0+)
capabilities.resolution: HARD LIMIT — verbatim: 'Core Location prevents any single app from monitoring more than 20 conditions of any type simultaneously.' Same 20 as legacy CLRegion; CLMonitor did NOT raise it. Limit is per-app across all CLMonitor instances. Community: expect entry/exit notification within 3–5 minutes on average; 1–400 m radius works best (twocentstudios, unverified by Apple).
capabilities.backfill: none — but CLMonitor PERSISTS its conditions across launches under the monitor's name, and record(for:)?.lastEvent replays the last known state per condition
capabilities.notes: Relaunch: 'If an iOS app isn't running when a condition is satisfied, the system tries to launch it. When the app relaunches, recreate the monitor with the same identifier. Note that monitoring can only occur after the user unlocks the device after a reboot.' — this is the ONLY CoreLocation API where Apple states the first-unlock-after-reboot requirement explicitly. FIELD CRASH: recreating a CLMonitor with the same name too soon after discarding the previous instance throws 'Monitor named X is already in use' — which is exactly the relaunch path Apple instructs you to take. Subscribe to .events ONCE per instance; you cannot cancel and resubscribe.

capabilities.stream: Geofence enter/exit (LEGACY region monitoring — still functional, deprecated in iOS 27 beta)
capabilities.api: CLCircularRegion(center:radius:identifier:); CLLocationManager.startMonitoring(for:) {DEPRECATED}, stopMonitoring(for:) {DEPRECATED}, requestState(for:) {DEPRECATED}, monitoredRegions, maximumRegionMonitoringDistance; delegate didEnterRegion / didExitRegion / didDetermineState:for: / monitoringDidFailFor:withError: / didStartMonitoringFor:; CLRegion.notifyOnEntry, .notifyOnExit; CLRegionState: unknown, inside, outside
capabilities.permission: Always required for relaunch; WhenInUse delivers only while in use
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 7.0+ — CLCircularRegion is DEPRECATED@27.0 (iOS 27 beta, verified 2026-07-24), replaced by CLCircularGeographicCondition. startMonitoring(for:) already listed under CoreLocation 'Deprecated symbols'
capabilities.resolution: Exactly 20 regions per app: 'Core Location limits to 20 the number of regions that may be simultaneously monitored by a single app.' Radius ceiling = maximumRegionMonitoringDistance (returns -1 if unavailable); exceeding it yields CLError.regionMonitoringFailure. Latency (archived Apple guide): 'the user's location must cross the region boundary, move away from the boundary by a minimum distance, and remain at that minimum distance for at least 20 seconds before the notifications are reported' and 'For testing purposes, you can assume that the minimum distance is approximately 200 meters.'
capabilities.backfill: none — but region registrations persist: 'The location manager persists region data between launches of your app. If your app is terminated and then relaunched, the contents of this property are repopulated with region objects that contain the previously registered data.'
capabilities.notes: CONTRADICTION IN APPLE'S OWN DOCS on reboot: the condition-monitoring article says 'The system monitors your conditions until you explicitly ask it to stop or until the DEVICE REBOOTS', while monitoredRegions says registrations persist across launches, and the CLMonitor article says monitoring resumes after first unlock post-reboot. Safest engineering read: re-register on every launch and don't rely on either claim. Archived guide on relaunch: 'In iOS, regions associated with your app are tracked at all times, including when the app isn't running. If a region boundary is crossed while an app isn't running, that app is relaunched into the background to handle the event.'

capabilities.stream: Presence of a specific iBeacon (enter/exit)
capabilities.api: CLMonitor.BeaconIdentityCondition(uuid:) / (uuid:major:) / (uuid:major:minor:) — ObjC class CLBeaconIdentityCondition. LEGACY: CLBeaconRegion {DEPRECATED@27.0}, CLBeaconIdentityConstraint {DEPRECATED@27.0}, CLBeaconRegion.notifyEntryStateOnDisplay, peripheralData(withMeasuredPower:); CLBeaconMajorValue, CLBeaconMinorValue
capabilities.permission: Same location prompts; also requires Bluetooth to be on
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 17.0+ for the Condition form; iOS 7.0+ for CLBeaconRegion (deprecated@27.0, iOS 27 beta)
capabilities.resolution: Identity = UUID (required) + major + minor. Omitted major/minor act as wildcards. Counts against the SAME 20-condition budget as geofences.
capabilities.notes: Practical life-logging use: a cheap iBeacon in your car / at your desk gives sub-room-level presence that no GPS geofence can resolve, at near-zero power. CLLocationManager.isMonitoringAvailable(for:) and isRangingAvailable() gate availability.

capabilities.stream: Distance to a nearby iBeacon (CLBeacon: proximity, accuracy, rssi, uuid, major, minor, timestamp)
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.startRangingBeacons(satisfying:) / stopRangingBeacons(satisfying:) / rangedBeaconConstraints; delegate locationManager(_:didRange:satisfying:) and didFailRangingFor:error:; CLProximity: unknown, immediate, near, far
capabilities.permission: Location prompt + Bluetooth
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 13.0+ for the (satisfying:) form; startRangingBeacons(in:) iOS 7.0+ {DEPRECATED}
capabilities.resolution: proximity is a 4-bucket enum; accuracy is meters-from-beacon (explicitly NOT a location accuracy); rssi in decibels
capabilities.notes: Ranging is a foreground/in-use activity: it does not relaunch a terminated app and stops when the app suspends. It is the only beacon mode giving a continuous distance signal, and the one that will not survive backgrounding — so pair monitoring (background, relaunches) with ranging (foreground, precise) rather than choosing one.

capabilities.stream: Compass heading (CLHeading: magneticHeading, trueHeading, headingAccuracy, x, y, z, timestamp)
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.startUpdatingHeading() / stopUpdatingHeading() / headingFilter / headingOrientation {DEPRECATED@27.0} / heading / headingAvailable() / dismissHeadingCalibrationDisplay(); delegate locationManager(_:didUpdateHeading:) and locationManagerShouldDisplayHeadingCalibration(_:); CLDeviceOrientation; CLHeadingComponentValue; kCLHeadingFilterNone
capabilities.permission: Location authorization; NOTE trueHeading is only populated if you ALSO run location updates
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 3.0+
capabilities.resolution: Degrees. headingFilter = minimum angular change (degrees) to emit; kCLHeadingFilterNone reports all. x/y/z are raw geomagnetic microteslas — a genuine raw-sensor stream, useful for detecting indoor magnetic signatures.
capabilities.notes: Verbatim: 'Heading information is available only on devices with a built-in magnetometer; it's not available in iOS Simulator.' And: 'If you want heading objects to contain valid data for the trueHeading property, configure your location manager object to deliver location updates.' Declare UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities 'magnetometer' if required. iOS 27 beta adds CLLocationManager.headingBody: (any CLBodyIdentifiable)? — heading relative to a non-Earth body; both symbols are iOS 27.0 BETA as of 2026-07-24 and may change before September.

capabilities.stream: Course, speed, altitude, floor and provenance riding along on every CLLocation
capabilities.api: CLLocation.course, courseAccuracy, speed, speedAccuracy, altitude, ellipsoidalAltitude, verticalAccuracy, floor (CLFloor.level), sourceInformation (CLLocationSourceInformation.isSimulatedBySoftware, .isProducedByAccessory), timestamp, distance(from:); typealiases CLLocationSpeed, CLLocationDirection, CLLocationSpeedAccuracy, CLLocationDirectionAccuracy
capabilities.permission: none beyond the location prompt that produced the CLLocation
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 2.0+ (ellipsoidalAltitude iOS 15.0+; sourceInformation iOS 15.0+; floor iOS 8.0+; courseAccuracy/speedAccuracy iOS 13.4+)
capabilities.resolution: speed m/s; course degrees from true north; altitude meters above mean sea level; ellipsoidalAltitude meters above the WGS84 ellipsoid; CLFloor.level is a logical building floor (only populated in mapped venues such as airports and malls)
capabilities.notes: These are FREE — you already paid the power cost to get the fix. Course is direction of TRAVEL and is independent of heading (device orientation); confusing the two is the classic bug. isSimulatedBySoftware is the data-quality filter that keeps GPX-simulated fixes out of a log you intend to trust — Apple explicitly suggests rejecting locations where it is true outside of debugging. CLFloor is the only vertical-indoor signal CoreLocation exposes.

capabilities.stream: One-shot current position
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.requestLocation()
capabilities.permission: Location prompt
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 9.0+
capabilities.resolution: Single fix at desiredAccuracy, then services stop automatically
capabilities.backfill: none — though CLLocationManager.location returns the last cached fix with no service start at all
capabilities.notes: 'If obtaining the desired accuracy would take too long, the location manager delivers a less accurate location value rather than reporting an error.' Calling startUpdatingLocation() cancels a pending requestLocation().

capabilities.stream: HISTORICAL location samples from before the app asked (the one genuine backfill in CoreLocation)
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.requestHistoricalLocations(purposeKey:sampleCount:completionHandler:) — async form historicalLocations(purposeKey:sampleCount:) async throws -> [CLLocation]. Failure code: CLError.historicalLocationError
capabilities.permission: purposeKey is a usage-description key (same pattern as requestTemporaryFullAccuracyAuthorization's NSLocationTemporaryUsageDescriptionDictionary); Apple's page publishes NO Discussion text confirming which plist dictionary it resolves against
capabilities.minIOS: watchOS 9.0+ ONLY — the platform table lists no iOS, iPadOS, macOS or visionOS availability at all
capabilities.backfill: YES — this is the sole CoreLocation API that returns samples predating your monitoring. Depth is UNDOCUMENTED: Apple publishes only the sampleCount parameter with no stated ceiling and no stated time window.
capabilities.resolution: Caller-specified sampleCount; granularity undocumented
capabilities.notes: Flagged deliberately because a blanket 'CoreLocation has no backfill' claim would be wrong. Apple's documentation for this method is effectively empty — abstract absent, no Discussion beyond the async-variant boilerplate. A developer-forum thread asking what it does (743341, Dec '23) has ZERO replies, including from Apple. Treat as watchOS-only, undocumented and unverified; the Apple Watch in the available hardware is the only reason this row exists.

capabilities.stream: Coordinate -> street address / place name (LEGACY, deprecated iOS 26)
capabilities.api: CLGeocoder.reverseGeocodeLocation(_:completionHandler:) / (_:preferredLocale:completionHandler:), geocodeAddressString(...), geocodePostalAddress(...), cancelGeocode(), isGeocoding -> CLPlacemark (name, thoroughfare, subThoroughfare, locality, subLocality, administrativeArea, subAdministrativeArea, postalCode, country, isoCountryCode, inlandWater, ocean, areasOfInterest, timeZone, postalAddress, region, location)
capabilities.permission: none — geocoding needs no location permission at all; you may geocode any coordinate
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 5.0, DEPRECATED@26.0 ('Use MapKit'). CLPlacemark DEPRECATED@27.0 ('Use either GeoToolbox.PlaceDescriptor or MapKit')
capabilities.resolution: CONTESTED RATE LIMIT. Apple, verbatim and qualitative only: 'Geocoding requests are rate-limited for each app... Send at most one geocoding request for any one user action... in a typical situation, you should not send more than one geocoding request per minute.' Failure surfaces as CLError.network. Apple has NEVER published a number. Empirically, the backing service returns 'Throttled "PlaceRequest.REQUEST_TYPE_REVERSE_GEOCODING" request: Tried to make more than 50 requests in 60 seconds' with maxRequests=50, windowSize=60 — a developer-reported string, not an Apple commitment. Both figures should be treated as live: Apple's 1/minute is guidance, 50/60s is the observed server ceiling.
capabilities.notes: Explicitly not a background API — Apple: 'Do not start a geocoding request at a time when the user will not see the results immediately. For example, do not start a request if your application is inactive or in the background.' Offline capability is narrow and explicitly stated: 'the geocoder stores enough information locally to report the localized COUNTRY OR REGION NAME AND ISO COUNTRY CODE for many locations' — everything else requires network.

capabilities.stream: Coordinate -> named place (MODERN replacement, iOS 26+)
capabilities.api: MKReverseGeocodingRequest(location:) -> mapItems / getMapItems(completionHandler:), isLoading, isCancelled, cancel(), preferredLocale. Forward: MKGeocodingRequest(addressString:) with region + preferredLocale. Results: MKMapItem, MKAddress, MKAddressRepresentations
capabilities.permission: none
capabilities.resolution: CONTESTED, and sharper than CLGeocoder's. Apple's MKReverseGeocodingRequest page documents NO rate limit at all. Apple DTS engineer Kevin Elliott, verbatim: 'Both APIs are built on the same underlying SPI and I believe their limits are broadly similar' and 'I believe it will return MKError.Code.loadingThrottled if you hit the limit.' Note the hedging — this is DTS opinion, not documentation. So: same ~50/60s ceiling as CLGeocoder, different error type (MKError.loadingThrottled vs CLError.network), and zero documentation.
capabilities.notes: This is the API to build against — CLGeocoder is deprecated as of iOS 26 and CLPlacemark as of iOS 27 beta. Returns MKMapItem (with pointOfInterestCategory, phoneNumber, url, timeZone), which is strictly richer than CLPlacemark.

capabilities.stream: Stable identity for a place across months (so 'my office' survives without re-geocoding)
capabilities.api: MKMapItem.identifier: MKMapItem.Identifier?, MKMapItem.alternateIdentifiers: Set<MKMapItem.Identifier>, MKMapItem.Identifier(identifierString:); MKMapItemRequest(mapItemIdentifier:) -> getMapItem(completionHandler:); also MKMapItemRequest(placeDescriptor:); MKMapItem.name, pointOfInterestCategory, phoneNumber, url, timeZone, isCurrentLocation, forCurrentLocation(), init(location:address:)
capabilities.permission: none
capabilities.minIOS: MKMapItem.Identifier iOS 18.0+; MKMapItemRequest iOS 16.0+ (the mapItemIdentifier: initializer accompanies Identifier); init(location:address:) and placeDescriptor iOS 26.0+
capabilities.resolution: MKPointOfInterestCategory has exactly 84 constants: museum, musicVenue, theater, library, planetarium, school, university, movieTheater, nightlife, fireStation, hospital, pharmacy, police, castle, fortress, landmark, nationalMonument, bakery, brewery, cafe, distillery, foodMarket, restaurant, winery, animalService, atm, automotiveRepair, bank, beauty, evCharger, fitnessCenter, laundry, mailbox, postOffice, restroom, spa, store, amusementPark, aquarium, beach, campground, fairground, marina, nationalPark, park, rvPark, zoo, baseball, basketball, bowling, goKart, golf, hiking, miniGolf, rockClimbing, skatePark, skating, skiing, soccer, stadium, tennis, volleyball, airport, carRental, conventionCenter, gasStation, hotel, parking, publicTransport, fishing, kayaking, surfing, swimming, airportTerminal, automotiveDealership, commercialVehicleDealership, informationBooth, motorbikeDealership, picnicArea, rangerStation, restArea, scenicView, ticketOffice, visitorCenter
capabilities.notes: THE key architectural move for a life-log. MKMapItem.Identifier is archivable (init(identifierString:)) and MKMapItemRequest(mapItemIdentifier:) resolves it back to a full MKMapItem later. So you geocode a visit centroid ONCE, store the identifier string, and never spend throttle budget on that place again. Re-resolution is still a network call, but it is cheap, cacheable and idempotent — which is what makes a multi-year place log tractable under a ~50/60s ceiling.

capabilities.stream: Portable place descriptor for cross-service place resolution
capabilities.api: PlaceDescriptor(representations:commonName:supportingRepresentations:), PlaceDescriptor(item: MKMapItem), .commonName, .address, .coordinate, .representations, .supportingRepresentations, .serviceIdentifier(for:); PlaceDescriptor.PlaceRepresentation, PlaceDescriptor.SupportingPlaceRepresentation
capabilities.permission: none
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 26.0+ (entire framework is new in iOS 26)
capabilities.resolution: n/a — it is a descriptor, not a lookup
capabilities.notes: Easy to mistake for an offline place database. It is NOT: verbatim, 'Use PlaceDescriptor in conjunction with A MAPPING SERVICE to request rich information about a place.' Its real value for an ownership-minded build is serviceIdentifier(for:) and supportingRepresentations, which carry third-party providers' own place IDs — i.e. it is the documented seam for resolving a place against a NON-Apple mapping service (OSM/Overture/your own) instead of Apple's throttled one. Also the named successor to CLPlacemark in iOS 27 beta's deprecation banner.

capabilities.stream: Nearby POI search / autocomplete (to name a place from its surroundings)
capabilities.api: MKLocalSearch(request:) with MKLocalSearch.Request or MKLocalPointsOfInterestRequest, start(completionHandler:), isSearching, cancel(), MKLocalSearch.Response, MKLocalSearch.ResultType; MKLocalSearchCompleter with queryFragment, region, regionPriority, resultTypes, pointOfInterestFilter, addressFilter, results, isSearching, cancel()
capabilities.permission: none
capabilities.minIOS: MKLocalSearch iOS 6.1+; MKLocalSearchCompleter iOS 9.3+
capabilities.resolution: Server-backed; same undocumented throttling family
capabilities.notes: The practical fallback when reverse geocoding returns a street address but you want the BUSINESS at that address — search MKLocalPointsOfInterestRequest around the visit centroid and take the nearest match whose pointOfInterestCategory is plausible. This is how you turn a CLVisit centroid into 'Starbucks on Preston' rather than '4123 Preston Rd'.

capabilities.stream: Server-initiated location query while the app is not running
capabilities.api: CLLocationPushServiceExtension protocol; CLLocationManager.startMonitoringLocationPushes(completion:) / stopMonitoringLocationPushes(); CLLocationPushServiceError + .Code; CLLocationPushServiceErrorDomain
capabilities.permission: Always authorization REQUIRED, plus APNs registration; apns-topic = <bundleID>.location-query, apns-push-type = location
capabilities.entitlement: REQUIRED — com.apple.developer.location.push. Verbatim: 'Without this entitlement, your code receives an error when it calls startMonitoringLocationPushes(completion:).' This is the ONLY signed entitlement in the entire CoreLocation surface.
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 15.0+ (the entitlement key page lists iOS 7.0+ / macOS 10.9+, a documentation artifact — the LPSE feature itself is 'available starting in iOS 15')
capabilities.resolution: Quota, verbatim: 'The system limits the number of push events a device may receive to approximately 360 events in a 24-hour period... the system also replenishes them at a rate of 1 every few minutes, up to the maximum daily allotment... There's no way to find out how many push events are remaining at any given time.' If capacity is exhausted the system unregisters from the push topic entirely for a period.
capabilities.notes: For a single-user self-installed life-logger this is the wrong tool AND the one real wall: it requires a signed entitlement, an APNs-capable server, and Apple's stated eligibility framing (location-sharing between approved people, or emergency first-responder alerting). Named here for completeness of the entitlement question, not as a recommended path.

capabilities.stream: Authorization and accuracy state (the metadata that determines whether any of the above is actually running)
capabilities.api: CLLocationManager.authorizationStatus, accuracyAuthorization, locationServicesEnabled(), isAuthorizedForWidgetUpdates, requestWhenInUseAuthorization(), requestAlwaysAuthorization(), requestTemporaryFullAccuracyAuthorization(withPurposeKey:) and (withPurposeKey:completion:); delegate locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization(_:). CLAuthorizationStatus: notDetermined, restricted, denied, authorizedAlways, authorizedWhenInUse (+ deprecated static `authorized`). CLAccuracyAuthorization: fullAccuracy, reducedAccuracy
capabilities.permission: Info.plist keys, all of them: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription (required), NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription (required for Always), NSLocationTemporaryUsageDescriptionDictionary (required for temporary full accuracy), NSLocationDefaultAccuracyReduced (optional Boolean), NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription {DEPRECATED@10.0}, NSLocationUsageDescription {DEPRECATED, macOS}, CLRequireExplicitServiceSession / NSLocationRequireExplicitServiceSession (optional)
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 2.0+ (accuracy authorization and temporary full accuracy iOS 14.0+; isAuthorizedForWidgetUpdates iOS 14.0+)
capabilities.resolution: Reduced accuracy is roughly city-block-to-neighbourhood scale (kCLLocationAccuracyReduced). Setting NSLocationDefaultAccuracyReduced=true degrades EVERYTHING, verbatim: 'all Core Location services (location updates, visit monitoring, significant location change, fence monitoring) receive service at the reduced-accuracy service level.'
capabilities.notes: THE PROVISIONAL-ALWAYS FLOW, verbatim from requestAlwaysAuthorization(): calling it from notDetermined produces TWO prompts. Prompt 1 uses NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription; choosing 'Allow While Using App' grants 'a Provisional Always authorization. The delegate receives authorizedAlways.' Prompt 2 arrives unrequested later: 'The second prompt displays when Core Location prepares to deliver an event to your app requiring authorizedAlways... Core Location will typically display the second prompt when your app ISN'T RUNNING.' Choosing 'Change to Always Allow' makes it permanent and the delegate gets NO callback. Also: 'Core Location limits calls to requestAlwaysAuthorization(). After your app calls this method, further calls have no effect.' — one shot, ever. DOC CONTRADICTION: this page says you need NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription, which Apple separately marks DEPRECATED@10.0; the authorization article says NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription. Ship both keys.

blockers: FREE APPLE ID, 7-DAY WALL — the dominant practical constraint here, and it is NOT a CoreLocation limit. Nothing in CoreLocation except Location Push needs a signed entitlement (UIBackgroundModes:location is an Info.plist array value, not an entitlement), so a personal team can build the whole thing. But free personal-team provisioning profiles expire ~7 days after issuance, after which the app will not launch. For an app whose entire premise is uninterrupted multi-week background monitoring, the log stops every week until you re-sign from Xcode. Apple's own help page confirms profiles 'may require you to rebuild and re-install your app to your device after expiration.' Budget for a weekly re-deploy, or pay the $99 developer-program fee for 1-year profiles. NOT verified: whether re-signing preserves CLMonitor's persisted conditions and the app's Always authorization — Apple documents neither; assume both may reset and re-register on every launch.

iOS's own 'Significant Locations' history (Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > Significant Locations) is NOT readable by any third-party API. Proof of exhaustion: I enumerated every symbol on the CoreLocation framework index, CLLocationManager's complete topic sections, the Deprecated-symbols collection, and Core Location Constants — no read API for the system place history exists at any deprecation level. The similarly-named startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges() only monitors changes GOING FORWARD; it does not expose the system's stored list. You cannot bootstrap a place history from what iOS already knows about you.

NO BACKFILL on any iOS CoreLocation API. Every stream above starts empty on first launch — the log begins the day you install. The single exception is requestHistoricalLocations(...), which is watchOS 9.0+ ONLY and has no iOS availability whatsoever. This is the sharpest structural contrast with HealthKit, which returns years of prior data on day one.

OFFLINE PLACE NAMING IS NOT POSSIBLE beyond country + ISO code. Clustering CLVisit centroids into stable, repeat-visited places is pure arithmetic on lat/lon and works fully offline forever — that part is easy. NAMING them is not. Proof of exhaustion: CLGeocoder states only 'the localized country or region name and ISO country code' are stored locally; MKReverseGeocodingRequest / MKGeocodingRequest / MKLocalSearch / MKLocalSearchCompleter / MKMapItemRequest are all server-backed (they share the throttled PlaceRequest SPI); GeoToolbox.PlaceDescriptor is explicitly a descriptor to hand TO a mapping service, not a database; and Apple Maps' consumer offline-map downloads (iOS 17+) expose no third-party API — no MapKit class references them. The ownership-preserving workaround is to name each place ONCE online, persist the MKMapItem.Identifier string, and thereafter resolve locally from your own store — or resolve against a self-hosted OSM/Overture extract via PlaceDescriptor.serviceIdentifier(for:).

EXACTLY 20 MONITORED CONDITIONS PER APP, and CLMonitor did not raise it. Verbatim: 'Core Location prevents any single app from monitoring more than 20 conditions of any type simultaneously.' Geofences and beacon conditions share the same budget. A life-logger that wants to geofence every meaningful place in a person's life cannot do so declaratively; detect overflow via CLMonitor.Event.conditionLimitExceeded (iOS 18+) and rotate.

STANDARD LOCATION UPDATES DO NOT SURVIVE TERMINATION, no matter how they are configured. Verbatim: 'If your app is terminated, the delivery of new location events stops altogether.' allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates keeps you alive while backgrounded; it does not resurrect you. Only visits, significant-change and region/condition monitoring relaunch a terminated app, and only with Always authorization.

BACKGROUND APP REFRESH — CONTESTED, and it matters because a user-facing toggle can silently kill the log. Apple's archived Location and Maps Programming Guide states it flatly: 'When a user disables the Background App Refresh setting either globally or for your app, the significant-change location service doesn't relaunch your app. Further, while Background App Refresh is off an app doesn't receive significant-change or region monitoring events even when it's in the foreground.' AGAINST: this sentence does not appear anywhere in the CURRENT CoreLocation documentation I enumerated, a developer reported (Dec 2022, iOS 16) that disabling Background Refresh did not affect background location updates in practice, and the current UIApplication.backgroundRefreshStatus page describes only 'refresh tasks' with no mention of location. Unresolved. Defensive posture: check UIApplication.shared.backgroundRefreshStatus at launch and surface it to yourself, because if the old claim still holds, the failure is completely silent.

APPLE'S DOCS CONTRADICT THEMSELVES ON REBOOT. The condition-monitoring article: 'The system monitors your conditions until you explicitly ask it to stop or until the device reboots.' The monitoredRegions page: 'The location manager persists region data between launches of your app. If your app is terminated and then relaunched, the contents of this property are repopulated.' The CLMonitor article: 'monitoring can only occur after the user unlocks the device after a reboot' — i.e. it resumes, but only post-first-unlock. These cannot all be literally true. For visits, significant-change and liveUpdates, Apple's documentation is SILENT on reboot entirely (checked startMonitoringVisits, startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges, CLVisit, CLLocationUpdate, handling-location-updates-in-the-background, requesting-authorization-to-use-location-services). Only safe design: re-register everything unconditionally on every launch, and never assume a reboot preserved state.

FORCE-QUIT (swipe-up from the app switcher) — CONTESTED, and Apple never uses the phrase in current documentation. Apple's current wording covers only 'terminated', which it treats uniformly: Always-authorized apps relaunch for visits, significant-change and region monitoring; nothing relaunches for standard updates. AGAINST a uniform reading: long-standing community reports hold that a USER-initiated force-quit is treated differently from a system eviction and suppresses relaunch until the next reboot or manual launch, and that startUpdatingLocation() specifically never relaunches while the other services usually do. I could not find an Apple DTS engineer on the record resolving this — the forum thread that asks the question verbatim ('Do user-terminated apps relaunch automatically for location changes?', thread 701377) has no Apple reply. Do not design around force-quit surviving; treat a user swipe-kill as an unrecoverable gap in the log and detect it by watching for time holes.

APPLE PUBLISHES NO ACCURACY OR LATENCY NUMBER FOR CLVisit. Not in CLVisit, not in startMonitoringVisits(), not in the power-optimization article. horizontalAccuracy is returned per-visit so you can filter, but there is no committed p50/p95 for how long after a real arrival the event fires. Anyone quoting a figure is reporting field observation, not documentation.

MKReverseGeocodingRequest's rate limit is entirely undocumented. Apple's page says nothing; the only guidance is a hedged DTS forum reply ('I believe their limits are broadly similar') and a developer-captured server string. You are building against an undocumented, unversioned ceiling that Apple can change without notice — which is precisely why the geocode-once/store-identifier architecture matters.
nonObvious: pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically DEFAULTS TO TRUE on iOS, and under WhenInUse a pause is permanent. Verbatim: 'For apps that have in-use authorization, a pause to location updates ends access to location changes until the app launches again and is able to restart those updates.' The out-of-the-box configuration silently kills a long-running log the first time you sit still, with no error and no delegate failure. Apple's own prescribed workaround is counterintuitive — do NOT set it to true for battery; instead set it to FALSE and drop desiredAccuracy to kCLLocationAccuracyThreeKilometers when backgrounding. A competent dev reads 'pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically = true saves battery', leaves the default, and loses days of data.

CLBackgroundActivitySession (iOS 17+) lets a WhenInUse app behave like an Always app while it runs — background updates and monitoring events, in exchange for the blue indicator, with NO Always prompt ever shown. For a self-installed app whose owner is the subject, this is often the better trade: you skip the two-stage Always dance entirely and get a visible honest indicator. The catch is the boundary — CLBackgroundActivitySession keeps you ALIVE, it does not RELAUNCH you. Terminated + WhenInUse = dead until manual launch. So the correct architecture is both: CLBackgroundActivitySession for continuous fidelity while running, and visits/SLC under Always as the resurrection layer.

THE VISITS/SLC RELAUNCH ASYMMETRY. Both relaunch a terminated app, but visits says 'You don't need to call this method again to restart the delivery of visit events' while significant-change says 'you MUST still configure a location manager object and call this method to continue receiving location events.' Copy the SLC relaunch handler onto visits and it still works (calling it 'does no harm'); copy the visits handler onto SLC and the service dies permanently after the first relaunch. Same doc family, opposite contracts, and nothing flags the difference.

VISITS RUN AT REDUCED ACCURACY WITH NO PRECISE-LOCATION REQUEST AT ALL. Verbatim: 'Your app can monitor for visit events without calling requestTemporaryPreciseLocationAuthorization(withPurposeKey:).' You can build a genuinely useful whole-life place log while the user's Precise Location toggle is OFF — the arrival/departure structure survives, only the centroid radius widens. Almost nobody builds this way because the assumption is that place-logging demands precise location.

GEOCODE ONCE, STORE MKMapItem.Identifier, RE-RESOLVE FOREVER. MKMapItem.Identifier is archivable via init(identifierString:) and MKMapItemRequest(mapItemIdentifier:) resolves it back to a full named MKMapItem. Under an undocumented ~50-requests-per-60-seconds ceiling, this is the difference between a place log that scales to years and one that throttles out in month two. The naive design reverse-geocodes every visit; the correct one reverse-geocodes each NEW cluster centroid once, persists the identifier string, and never pays again.

ROTATE THE 20 CONDITIONS BY DISTANCE TO FAKE UNLIMITED GEOFENCES. The 20-condition cap is per-app-simultaneous, not per-app-total. Keep the full place list in your own store, and on every significant-change event (which costs nothing extra — you're already relaunched) re-add the 20 nearest conditions and remove the rest. CLMonitor.Event.conditionLimitExceeded (iOS 18+) tells you when you have overflowed. This is the standard trick behind every commercial geofencing SDK and it is invisible from the API surface.

CLMonitor CRASHES ON EXACTLY THE PATH APPLE TELLS YOU TO TAKE. Apple says: on relaunch, 'recreate the monitor with the same identifier.' In the field, recreating a CLMonitor with the same name too soon after discarding the previous instance throws 'Monitor named X is already in use'. Since relaunch-and-recreate is the entire background story for CLMonitor, this fires on the hot path. Related: subscribe to CLMonitor.events exactly ONCE per instance — you cannot cancel and resubscribe, and a second concurrent subscription distributes events randomly between them. (Field reports, twocentstudios 2024-12-02; not documented by Apple.)

iBEACONS BEAT GEOFENCES FOR THE PLACES THAT MATTER MOST. A CLMonitor.BeaconIdentityCondition triggers on a Bluetooth beacon's presence, works indoors where GPS geofences are useless, resolves to a room rather than a ~200 m circle, relaunches a terminated app the same way a geofence does, and costs almost nothing in power. For a personal quantified-self build, a $15 beacon on your desk and one in your car produces cleaner arrival/departure data than any geofence radius you could tune — and it is the only way to distinguish 'at the office building' from 'at my desk'.

CLHeading EXPOSES RAW MAGNETOMETER MICROTESLAS (x, y, z), not just a compass bearing. Indoor environments have distinctive magnetic signatures from steel structure and electrical loads, so the raw vector is a usable place-fingerprint where GPS is degraded — a signal no other CoreLocation API surfaces. Note trueHeading stays invalid unless you ALSO run location updates.

CLLocationSourceInformation.isSimulatedBySoftware IS A DATA-INTEGRITY GATE, and Apple explicitly suggests using it: 'an app may choose to check the source information and reject locations if the isSimulatedBySoftware property is true when the developer isn't debugging or testing the app.' For a log you intend to trust years from now, filtering simulated fixes at write time is the difference between a clean corpus and one silently contaminated by every Xcode GPX debug session.

CLFloor.level IS FREE VERTICAL CONTEXT you never asked for — it rides along on CLLocation inside mapped venues (airports, malls, large transit hubs) at no power cost. Most developers never read it because it is nil almost everywhere, but in exactly the places where a life-log is otherwise ambiguous ('which terminal?'), it resolves the ambiguity for zero effort.

THE ALWAYS PROMPT IS ONE-SHOT AND ITS SECOND HALF ARRIVES UNREQUESTED, WHILE YOUR APP IS NOT RUNNING. 'Core Location limits calls to requestAlwaysAuthorization(). After your app calls this method, further calls have no effect.' And the confirmation prompt 'will typically display the second prompt when your app isn't running.' If the owner taps 'Keep Only While Using' on that surprise prompt days later, you drop to WhenInUse, you lose terminated-app relaunch, and you can never ask again from code — recovery is a manual trip to Settings. Detect the downgrade in locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization and surface it loudly, because otherwise the log just quietly stops resurrecting itself.

THE FATAL-ERROR TRAP: allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates = true without UIBackgroundModes containing 'location' is not a warning or a no-op — verbatim, it 'is a fatal error that terminates the app.' It is the one CoreLocation misconfiguration that crashes rather than degrades.

iOS 27 (beta 4 as of 2026-07-24) COMPLETES THE LEGACY PURGE: CLCircularRegion, CLBeaconRegion, CLBeaconIdentityConstraint, CLPlacemark and CLLocationManager.headingOrientation are all marked DEPRECATED@27.0, following CLGeocoder's deprecation in iOS 26. Beta markers can move before the September release, so treat these as directional rather than final. New in iOS 27 beta: the CLBodyIdentifiable protocol and CLLocationManager.headingBody — heading relative to a body other than Earth, implying non-terrestrial reference frames are coming to the heading stack. Net: build on CLMonitor + CLCircularGeographicCondition + MKReverseGeocodingRequest today; every CLRegion/CLGeocoder tutorial online is now describing a deprecated path.
